why_this_type.zh-CN: 这次{{dominant_axis_label}}的作答方向更偏向{{dominant_side_label}}，它参与组成当前代码。可以先找一个符合和一个不符合的经历，看看这条描述是否有用。{{identity_clause}}
why_this_type.en: You land in this type not because you must perform like a stereotype at all times, but because {{dominant_axis_label}} and {{dominant_side_label}} keep pulling you back to the same judgment entry point. {{close_axis_label}} still gives your surface rhythm elasticity, which is why you look more layered than a template. {{identity_clause}}

misunderstanding_fix.zh-CN: 不同的自我描述可能与情境、已学会的行为或措辞有关。请比较{{dominant_side_label}}及另一侧的具体例子；这份结果不证明你最后总会回到同一判断方式。{{identity_clause}}
misunderstanding_fix.en: When people occasionally misread you, it is usually not because the result is wrong, but because {{close_axis_label}} leaves room for your expression to switch. You may not look like a textbook {{dominant_side_label}} on the surface, but your actual judgment still returns there. {{identity_clause}}

why_this_type.zh-CN: 主类型成立的核心证据很简单：{{dominant_axis_label}}上的{{dominant_side_label}}持续占上风。{{close_axis_label}}会影响你看起来像谁，但不会改写你最终怎么判断。{{identity_clause}}
why_this_type.en: The core evidence is simple: {{dominant_axis_label}} and {{dominant_side_label}} keep winning. {{close_axis_label}} can change how you look on the surface, but not how you close judgment. {{identity_clause}}

misunderstanding_fix.zh-CN: 别人误读你，多半是把{{close_axis_label}}上的波动当成主类型变化。真正要抓住的是：你最终还是回到{{dominant_side_label}}的判断入口，而不是一直停在摇摆里。{{identity_clause}}
misunderstanding_fix.en: People usually misread you by treating movement around {{close_axis_label}} as a type change. The real point is that you still come back to {{dominant_side_label}} for final judgment instead of staying in drift. {{identity_clause}}

why_this_type.zh-CN: 回看{{dominant_axis_label}}，本次回答更偏向{{dominant_side_label}}。它是解释当前代码的一条线索；把一段符合的经历和一段反例并排记录，再判断它在什么情境下有解释力。{{identity_clause}}
why_this_type.en: If you look back across phases of your life, the outer expression can shift, but {{dominant_axis_label}} and {{dominant_side_label}} still remain your most stable return path. {{close_axis_label}} explains why you do not look like a single template, not why you do not belong here. {{identity_clause}}

misunderstanding_fix.zh-CN: 不同的自我描述可能与情境、已学会的行为或措辞有关。请比较{{dominant_side_label}}及另一侧的具体例子；这份结果不证明你最后总会回到同一判断方式。{{identity_clause}}
misunderstanding_fix.en: Looking somewhat different across contexts does not mean the core type keeps changing. It is closer to {{close_axis_label}} borrowing different rhythms at different times. What stays stable is that you still return to {{dominant_side_label}} as the main judgment line. {{identity_clause}}

why_this_type.zh-CN: 先把当前代码当作整理本次回答的暂时入口：{{dominant_axis_label}}显示较偏向{{dominant_side_label}}的方向。可以稍后用具体经历再核对，无需急着固定身份。{{identity_clause}}
why_this_type.en: When your recent state has felt more volatile, the important thing is not to re-doubt the core type, but to hold onto the stable axis: {{dominant_axis_label}} and {{dominant_side_label}} are still here. {{close_axis_label}} can make your surface behavior fluctuate, but that explains switching, not a broken core. {{identity_clause}}

misunderstanding_fix.zh-CN: 不同的自我描述可能与情境、已学会的行为或措辞有关。请比较{{dominant_side_label}}及另一侧的具体例子；这份结果不证明你最后总会回到同一判断方式。{{identity_clause}}
misunderstanding_fix.en: The main risk right now is treating state fluctuation as type distortion. {{close_axis_label}} can absolutely make your expression wobble, but the judgment entry point that defines you has not disappeared. {{identity_clause}}

adjacent_type_contrast.zh-CN: {{neighbor_type}}是跨过{{axis_label}}当前归类方向后可比较的标签。请核对{{side_label}}和{{opposite_side_label}}的具体例子；相似感不证明其中一个标签就是固定的你。
adjacent_type_contrast.en: You can look a little like {{neighbor_type}} because {{axis_label}} sits close enough to the middle that your surface rhythm occasionally borrows {{opposite_side_label}}. What separates you is that you still come back to {{side_label}} to close judgment.

misunderstanding_fix.zh-CN: {{neighbor_type}}只是一个比较入口，不是别人一定会把你看成的类型。请比较{{side_label}}与{{opposite_side_label}}的具体例子，不从外在相似推断内在判断。{{identity_clause}}
misunderstanding_fix.en: So there is no need to read that similarity as “the result must be wrong.” It is closer to a near-boundary axis preserving expressive elasticity than to the core type being overturned. {{identity_clause}}

adjacent_type_contrast.zh-CN: 别人把你看成{{neighbor_type}}，关键原因就是{{axis_label}}太靠近中线，外显风格会短暂像{{opposite_side_label}}。但真正决定类型归属的，是你最后还是回到{{side_label}}完成判断。
adjacent_type_contrast.en: People read you as {{neighbor_type}} mainly because {{axis_label}} sits too close to the middle, so the surface briefly looks like {{opposite_side_label}}. What decides the type is that you still return to {{side_label}} for closure.

misunderstanding_fix.zh-CN: 别把表面像不像当成核心证据。真正有效的判断标准，是你最后用哪一侧完成决策和收尾。{{identity_clause}}
misunderstanding_fix.en: Do not treat surface resemblance as the decisive evidence. The real standard is which side you use to complete judgment and closure. {{identity_clause}}

adjacent_type_contrast.zh-CN: {{neighbor_type}}是跨过{{axis_label}}当前归类方向后可比较的标签。请核对{{side_label}}和{{opposite_side_label}}的具体例子；相似感不证明其中一个标签就是固定的你。
adjacent_type_contrast.en: If you look back across different stages, the times when you were most easily read as {{neighbor_type}} usually trace back to {{axis_label}} being near the boundary. It changes who you resemble on the surface, but not the fact that you still end up leaning on {{side_label}} to complete judgment.

misunderstanding_fix.zh-CN: {{neighbor_type}}只是一个比较入口，不是别人一定会把你看成的类型。请比较{{side_label}}与{{opposite_side_label}}的具体例子，不从外在相似推断内在判断。{{identity_clause}}
misunderstanding_fix.en: This kind of misread is closer to a phase-dependent surface shift than to the core type constantly changing. The look can vary, but the underlying judgment track does not. {{identity_clause}}

adjacent_type_contrast.zh-CN: {{neighbor_type}}是跨过{{axis_label}}当前归类方向后可比较的标签。请核对{{side_label}}和{{opposite_side_label}}的具体例子；相似感不证明其中一个标签就是固定的你。
adjacent_type_contrast.en: When your state is less steady, you are more likely to look like {{neighbor_type}} because the near-boundary {{axis_label}} pushes your surface style toward {{opposite_side_label}} first. The stabilizing fact is that you still return to {{side_label}} to complete judgment.

misunderstanding_fix.zh-CN: {{neighbor_type}}只是一个比较入口，不是别人一定会把你看成的类型。请比较{{side_label}}与{{opposite_side_label}}的具体例子，不从外在相似推断内在判断。{{identity_clause}}
misunderstanding_fix.en: The important thing now is not to obsess over whether you “changed type,” but to notice which near-boundary axis is amplifying that illusion. That axis explains surface fluctuation, not identity drift. {{identity_clause}}

stability_explanation.zh-CN: 你不必要求自己在所有情境中都一样。这些轴的分数描述本次回答中的方向线索；它不是对长期稳定性或恢复能力的评定。
stability_explanation.en: Your stability is better understood as a capacity you can care for, not as a demand to never fluctuate. {{close_axis_label}} is the reminder that the core type remains, while different contexts can still push you into different entry points. {{identity_clause}}

stability_reframe.zh-CN: 可以把“我是否变了类型”暂时换成“眼下哪些条件需要照顾”。从一个负担较小的调整开始，再观察它是否适合当前处境。
stability_reframe.en: So the more useful reading is not “why am I unstable again,” but “what kind of recovery will let me return to the core type’s most natural rhythm.” {{identity_clause}}

stress_recovery.zh-CN: 如果眼下需要休息或调整，可以温和地试一个小动作：{{scene_side_hint}}。结合当前负荷和实际反馈，看看它是否有帮助。
stress_recovery.en: In recovery, a gentler entry point tends to work best first: {{scene_side_hint}}.

stability_explanation.zh-CN: 先分清分数与推论：这些轴的分数只反映这次回答的方向分离程度，不能证明你总会如何判断、应对压力或恢复。
stability_explanation.en: The key is not whether you are stable in the abstract, but which axis gets pulled off course by context first. {{close_axis_label}} is the place to manage first. {{identity_clause}}

stability_reframe.zh-CN: 选最近一个具体情境，写下发生了什么、你怎样回应、得到了什么反馈。只定一个可调整的下一步，不用把这次经历归结为固定类型。
stability_reframe.en: What works is not pushing harder, but spotting imbalance sooner and starting recovery before full overload. {{identity_clause}}

stress_recovery.zh-CN: 压力上来时，先核对当前负荷与可用支持。若条件允许，可以试一个小调整：{{scene_side_hint}}。记录实际反应，不要求立刻恢复。
stress_recovery.en: When pressure rises, do not explain first; do one move that brings you back online quickly: {{scene_side_hint}}.

stability_explanation.zh-CN: 如果你有不同阶段的记录，可以比较这些轴的分数在相似情境中是否仍有解释力。本次分数本身不能回答这种模式是否随时间保持。
stability_explanation.en: If you look back at earlier states, you will notice this is not random wobbling but a repeated switch in certain situations. {{close_axis_label}} explains that repeatable switching pattern. {{identity_clause}}

stability_reframe.zh-CN: 记下一件符合描述的事和一件反例，再看当时的任务、关系和负荷有什么不同。保留其他解释，让记录帮助你修正理解。
stability_reframe.en: So stability does not always mean staying unchanged; it often means noticing the switch earlier and bringing yourself back faster. {{identity_clause}}

stress_recovery.zh-CN: 可以先回看{{scene_side_hint}}是否曾在具体经历中有帮助。若没有这样的记录，就把它作为待验证的小尝试，而不是已证实有效的恢复方式。
stress_recovery.en: In recovery, return first to an entry point that has already worked for you before: {{scene_side_hint}}.

stability_explanation.zh-CN: 如果当前负荷较高，先不要用这些轴的分数给自己增加身份判断。它来自本次回答，不能确定状态变化的原因，也不衡量你的恢复能力。
stability_explanation.en: What matters most right now is reading this result as something that can be stabilized, not treating every fluctuation as identity distortion. {{close_axis_label}} marks a sensitive entry point, not a failed core type. {{identity_clause}}

stability_reframe.zh-CN: 先看能否减少一项可推迟的要求，或获得一点实际支持。选择一个可撤回的小调整，之后核对负荷与反馈；暂时不急着解释自己属于哪一类。
stability_reframe.en: Instead of asking why you got pulled off again, standardize the recovery move first. You need a repeatable way back to steadiness, not another proof that you should never fluctuate. {{identity_clause}}

stress_recovery.zh-CN: 可以先尝试一个降低当前负荷的小动作：{{scene_side_hint}}。再观察是否有帮助，不由本结果推断神经系统状态。
stress_recovery.en: Use a stabilizing entry point first in recovery: {{scene_side_hint}}. Get yourself back into a usable zone before attempting anything bigger.

next_action.zh-CN: 下一步不用一下做很大。先从一个更容易维持的小动作开始：{{scene_side_hint}}。
next_action.en: Your next move does not need to be huge. Start with a smaller action you can actually maintain: {{scene_side_hint}}.

action_experiment.zh-CN: 把它当成一个对自己友好的小实验：{{action_hint}}。记录是否实际尝试及得到的反馈，再决定要不要扩大。
action_experiment.en: Treat this as a self-supportive small experiment: {{action_hint}}. Make one visible shift before deciding whether to scale it up.

action_bridge_step.zh-CN: 先做桥接动作，不要求一步到位：{{action_hint}}。重点是把起点和下一步连起来。
action_bridge_step.en: Start with a bridge step instead of demanding instant completion: {{action_hint}}. The goal is simply to connect the current state to the next step.

revisit_resume.zh-CN: 如果你之前已经停过一次，先从上次最接近完成的位置重新接上：{{recovery_hint}}。
revisit_resume.en: If you have already paused once before, resume from the point that was closest to completion last time: {{recovery_hint}}.

next_action.zh-CN: 下一步先选一个可撤回的小尝试：{{scene_side_hint}}。记录能否实际完成和得到的反馈，再判断方向。
next_action.en: Do not keep thinking about the next step; do one move that validates direction immediately: {{scene_side_hint}}.

action_experiment.zh-CN: 把它压成一个能今天启动的实验：{{action_hint}}。先得到反馈，再决定是否继续扩大。
action_experiment.en: Compress this into an experiment you can start today: {{action_hint}}. Get feedback first, then decide whether to expand.

action_resistance_break.zh-CN: 如果某一步确实卡住了，可以先把它拆小：{{action_hint}}。试一次，再核对卡点是否改变。
action_resistance_break.en: What works best now is not more planning, but breaking the most stuck point first: {{action_hint}}.

action_momentum_start.zh-CN: 把动作缩小后试一次：{{action_hint}}。条件允许时再重复一次，比较两次的条件与反馈。
action_momentum_start.en: Build momentum first: {{action_hint}}. Two consecutive completions matter more than one oversized push.

next_action.zh-CN: 如果你有类似尝试的记录，可以先回看哪些条件曾有帮助，再选择是否延续这个做法：{{scene_side_hint}}。
next_action.en: The next step is best attached to a pattern you have already seen work before: {{scene_side_hint}}.

action_experiment.zh-CN: 把它收成一个可回看、可复盘的小实验：{{action_hint}}。重点不是快，而是让你下次还能接得上。
action_experiment.en: Turn it into a small experiment you can revisit and review: {{action_hint}}. The point is not speed, but making the next resumption easier.

revisit_resume.zh-CN: 如果你已经做过类似动作，这次不要从零开始，直接接上曾经有效的版本：{{recovery_hint}}。
revisit_resume.en: If you have done something similar before, do not restart from zero; reconnect to the version that already worked: {{recovery_hint}}.

adaptive_retry.zh-CN: 如果之前的做法卡住了，先换一种更适合现在状态的重试入口：{{action_hint}}。
adaptive_retry.en: If the earlier approach got stuck, switch to a retry path that fits your current state better: {{action_hint}}.

next_action.zh-CN: 如果当前负荷较高，下一步可以先缩小或暂缓：{{scene_side_hint}}。根据实际负担和反馈决定是否继续。
next_action.en: Your next step right now should stabilize you before it pushes you forward: {{scene_side_hint}}.

action_reset.zh-CN: 可以先试一个重置动作：{{recovery_hint}}。观察负荷和反馈是否变化，再决定继续、调整或暂停。
action_reset.en: Start with a reset move: {{recovery_hint}}. Whether the action can continue depends on bringing your state back first.

adaptive_reduce_pressure.zh-CN: 把动作先降压：{{recovery_hint}}。先让它重新变得可用，再谈效率。
adaptive_reduce_pressure.en: Lower the pressure on the action first: {{recovery_hint}}. Make it usable again before you worry about efficiency.

recovery_reset.zh-CN: 先补上恢复动作：{{recovery_hint}}。恢复不是绕路，是让后面的动作不再崩掉。
recovery_reset.en: Add the recovery move first: {{recovery_hint}}. Recovery is not detouring; it is what keeps the next action from collapsing.

next_action.zh-CN: 下一步尽量轻一点：{{scene_side_hint}}。先让动作重新发生，不要求立刻很像“认真执行”。
next_action.en: Keep the next step lighter: {{scene_side_hint}}. The first goal is to make the action happen again, not to perform it perfectly.

action_low_pressure_step.zh-CN: 先试一个负担较小的版本：{{action_hint}}。记录能否完成；若仍然费力，可以继续缩小或暂停。
action_low_pressure_step.en: Start with a lower-pressure version: {{action_hint}}. The lighter it feels, the easier it is to rebuild continuity.

adaptive_reduce_pressure.zh-CN: 如果现在一想到要推进就更累，先把动作缩到几乎不会触发抗拒：{{recovery_hint}}。
adaptive_reduce_pressure.en: If moving forward already feels draining, shrink the step until it barely triggers resistance: {{recovery_hint}}.

revisit_resume.zh-CN: 复访时也不用一次追回全部进度，先接回一个最轻的版本就够了：{{recovery_hint}}。
revisit_resume.en: On a revisit, you do not need to catch up on everything at once; reconnecting with the lightest version is enough first: {{recovery_hint}}.

watchout.zh-CN: 这部分可以作为一个温和的核对问题：{{scene_side_hint}}。先看看具体经历中是否出现过相应困难，再决定是否调整。
watchout.en: This section works best as a gentle reminder: under pressure, this is where you are most likely to get off balance. Notice it first, then decide how to correct it: {{scene_side_hint}}.

watchout_recovery_gap.zh-CN: 如果最近动作经常中断，可以核对负荷、步骤大小和休息支持是否合适：{{watchout_hint}}。先不把中断归因于坚持不足或恢复不足。
watchout_recovery_gap.en: If actions keep breaking lately, do not blame yourself for lacking discipline first; repair the recovery gap first: {{watchout_hint}}.

recovery_reset.zh-CN: 恢复动作不是奖励，而是让你重新有余量继续前进的前提：{{recovery_hint}}。
recovery_reset.en: Recovery is not a reward; it is the prerequisite that gives you enough margin to move forward again: {{recovery_hint}}.

watchout.zh-CN: 先核对这个可能的卡点：{{scene_side_hint}}。如果具体经历中确实存在，再选一个小调整。
watchout.en: This is the place most likely to pull you off course right now. Do not wait for it to grow; address it first: {{scene_side_hint}}.

watchout_overcontrol.zh-CN: 检查是否有不必要的控制步骤：{{watchout_hint}}。若确实增加了负担，可以试着放宽一处，并观察实际影响。
watchout_overcontrol.en: The bigger risk right now is overcontrol. Let the process be usable; it does not have to be fully locked down: {{watchout_hint}}.

watchout_avoidant_delay.zh-CN: 如果准备已经持续很久，可以核对还缺什么信息：{{watchout_hint}}。条件具备时试一个最小动作，再记录反馈。
watchout_avoidant_delay.en: Do not keep dressing delay up as preparation. Do one minimal move and break the waiting loop: {{watchout_hint}}.

watchout.zh-CN: 如果当前负荷较高，可以先核对这个线索：{{scene_side_hint}}。根据具体情况减少一项要求或寻求支持，再观察反馈。
watchout.en: What matters here is not pushing yourself harder, but noticing imbalance earlier so the state does not spiral into collapse: {{scene_side_hint}}.

watchout_recovery_gap.zh-CN: 如果休息或支持不足，可以把它作为一个待调整的条件：{{watchout_hint}}。试一个负担较小的安排，再观察是否有帮助，不预判后续努力会失效。
watchout_recovery_gap.en: The bigger danger now is not slower action, but letting recovery stay absent. Without recovery, the effort that follows will distort faster: {{watchout_hint}}.

recovery_reset.zh-CN: 把恢复当成正经步骤，而不是失败后的补救：{{recovery_hint}}。
recovery_reset.en: Treat recovery as a real step in the process, not as damage control after failure: {{recovery_hint}}.

career_next_step.zh-CN: 职业下一步不一定要一下定很大，可以先做一个小验证：{{scene_side_hint}}。再核对它是否符合实际任务和条件。
career_next_step.en: Your next career step does not need to be huge. Start by testing a smaller move that fits your work rhythm better: {{scene_side_hint}}.

work_scene_role_fit.zh-CN: 可以先询问角色的实际任务与责任边界：{{work_hint}}。再结合技能、资源和工作经历判断，不只依靠匹配感或头衔。
work_scene_role_fit.en: Check role fit first: {{work_hint}}. Fit matters more than title when it comes to sustaining good work.

work_scene_transition.zh-CN: 如果你正站在变化前面，先做一个过渡验证动作：{{work_hint}}。
work_scene_transition.en: If you are standing in front of a change, begin with one transition-validation move: {{work_hint}}.

career_next_step.zh-CN: 把职业下一步落到一个可逆的小验证上：{{scene_side_hint}}。用实际反馈判断它是否推进了当前目标。
career_next_step.en: Do not keep the next career step abstract. Validate the move most likely to change reality first: {{scene_side_hint}}.

work_scene_execution.zh-CN: 先询问实际的执行方式：{{work_hint}}。再结合任务、技能、资源和自己的经历核对，不预判机会一定合适或一定消耗你。
work_scene_execution.en: Check whether the execution style fits you first: {{work_hint}}. If the way of moving work forward mismatches you, even a good opportunity will drain you.

work_scene_pacing.zh-CN: 如果当前节奏带来困难，可以先核对任务量、期限和可用支持：{{work_hint}}。试一个小调整，再记录实际影响。
work_scene_pacing.en: When pacing is off, career judgment distorts too. Bring the speed back to a range you can sustain: {{work_hint}}.

career_next_step.zh-CN: 如果你有相关工作经历，可以回看哪些任务和条件曾经适合，再决定是否用一个小验证延续它：{{scene_side_hint}}。
career_next_step.en: The next career step is best attached to a high-fit pattern you have already verified before: {{scene_side_hint}}.

work_scene_transition.zh-CN: 如果你之前换过环境或角色，先回看当时真正帮助你稳住的支撑条件：{{work_hint}}。
work_scene_transition.en: If you have changed environments or roles before, look back first at the conditions that actually helped you stabilize then: {{work_hint}}.

work_scene_role_fit.zh-CN: 回看这个角色中的具体任务、反馈和所需支持：{{work_hint}}。把顺手感作为一条线索，同时核对技能要求与现实限制。
work_scene_role_fit.en: Do not only ask whether you can do it; look back at whether doing it kept feeling smoother over time. That difference is real role fit: {{work_hint}}.

relationship_practice.zh-CN: 这周的关系动作可以先温和一点：{{scene_side_hint}}。重点不是一次说到最完整，而是让对方更容易接住你的真实节奏。
relationship_practice.en: Keep this week’s relationship move a little gentler: {{scene_side_hint}}. The goal is not perfect expression, but making your real rhythm easier for the other person to receive.

relationship_bridge.zh-CN: 先搭桥，不急着一次解决全部问题：{{relationship_hint}}。
relationship_bridge.en: Build the bridge first; there is no need to solve everything at once: {{relationship_hint}}.

relationship_low_intensity_reconnect.zh-CN: 如果最近有点疏离，先用低强度重新连接就够了：{{relationship_hint}}。
relationship_low_intensity_reconnect.en: If things have felt distant lately, a low-intensity reconnection is enough to start: {{relationship_hint}}.

relationship_practice.zh-CN: 这周别再等气氛自己变好，先主动做一个关系动作：{{scene_side_hint}}。
relationship_practice.en: Do not wait for the atmosphere to improve on its own this week; make one relationship move yourself: {{scene_side_hint}}.

relationship_boundary_negotiation.zh-CN: 边界别再只放在心里，直接说出来：{{relationship_hint}}。
relationship_boundary_negotiation.en: Do not keep the boundary in your head only; say it directly: {{relationship_hint}}.

relationship_misread_repair.zh-CN: 如果已经出现误读，先修正误读本身，不要继续让猜测扩大：{{relationship_hint}}。
relationship_misread_repair.en: If a misread has already happened, repair the misread itself first instead of letting guesswork expand: {{relationship_hint}}.

relationship_practice.zh-CN: 如果你们曾有双方认可的互动方式，这周可以考虑再试一次：{{scene_side_hint}}。先确认对方是否愿意，再核对当前反馈。
relationship_practice.en: This week’s relationship move is best attached to an interaction pattern you already know can work: {{scene_side_hint}}.

relationship_misread_repair.zh-CN: 如果类似误会以前也出现过，可以回看是否有双方认为有帮助的沟通方式：{{relationship_hint}}。若有，再确认这次是否适用。
relationship_misread_repair.en: If a similar misunderstanding has happened before, reopen the conversation through the path that helped you realign most easily last time: {{relationship_hint}}.

relationship_low_intensity_reconnect.zh-CN: 如果双方都愿意，可以从一次较轻的小互动重新联系：{{relationship_hint}}。不预设过去自然的方式现在仍然合适。
relationship_low_intensity_reconnect.en: Reconnection does not have to be heavy; begin with a small interaction that used to feel natural for both of you: {{relationship_hint}}.

relationship_practice.zh-CN: 如果最近关系上的负荷比较高，这周的动作先以回稳为主：{{scene_side_hint}}。
relationship_practice.en: If relationship load has felt high lately, let this week’s move prioritize stabilization first: {{scene_side_hint}}.

relationship_conflict_recovery.zh-CN: 如果刚发生冲突，可以先商量是否需要暂停，以及何时再谈：{{relationship_hint}}。按双方的意愿和当前条件决定下一步。
relationship_conflict_recovery.en: Handle the post-conflict stabilization first instead of immediately moving into more issues: {{relationship_hint}}.

relationship_boundary_negotiation.zh-CN: 如果有边界需要表达，可以先选双方愿意谈的时机：{{relationship_hint}}。说明具体需要，并核对对方怎样理解。
relationship_boundary_negotiation.en: The boundary still needs to be spoken, but speak it in a way that reduces collateral damage first: {{relationship_hint}}.
